newsitem.title: UK: Cathay says ex-UK cargo not affected.
newsitem.headline: Cathay says ex-UK cargo not affected.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd air cargo moving ex-UK will be "totally unaffected" by the decision to suspend its Airbus Industrie A330-300 flights in Asia due to problems with the plane's Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines.
"There will be no buildup of cargo," a Cathay spokesman told Reuters.
He was replying to a question as to whether the move which affects the airline's 11 A33O-300s flying out of Hong Kong would affect transshipment there of ex-UK cargo for other Asian destinations.

Cathay is one of the top airlines moving air cargo from Britain to Hong Kong on both Boeing 747 freighters and as bellyhold cargo on passenger planes. Other carriers include British Airways Plc, Virgin Atlantic Airways and more recently Air China.
Air Hong Kong, 75 percent controlled by Cathay, operates freighter flights from Britain to Hong Kong.
At the same time, Hong Kong-based Dragonair -- a Cathay associate which also operates A330-300s -- has also decided to suspend its flights for the same reasons as Cathay.
